body.p: . src/xdm_sequence.c adds three sequence cell classes and sxml_sequence_test_emptiness; xdm.h and src/xdm.c are unchanged.

item.p: Ranges store the two int64_t bounds; an empty range is the empty sequence and a one-integer range an inline item, so a range cell always has two or more items. Members are computed in uint64_t; every index below 2^64 is readable. Only the count of INT64_MIN to INT64_MAX (2^64 items) does not fit: sxml_sequence_count raises XPDY0130 (XPath 4.0, implementation-dependent limit), as for a concatenation whose total passes 2^64 - 1.

Concatenations drop empty inputs, flatten nested concatenations and return a lone remaining part itself (retained). Part ends (items up to and including each part) are a cache filled in order as reads count the parts; get_item binary-searches the counted parts and asks each further part for the item before counting it, so a lazy part is read only as far as needed. Iteration uses part_index/next_index_in_part: O(1) per item.

Lazy sequences keep produced items in a doubling array (room is made before calling the generator, so an item is never lost and an allocation failure is retryable). The generator always gets the cell's own error record; a failure is final: its error is copied into the cell (the kept error, ) and raised again through the heap by every later read that needs an item past the last produced one; items before it stay readable. A non-error status (out of memory in the generator) is kept and returned the same way. The generator's state is released only when the cell is freed, as xdm.h says. A generator that reads its own lazy sequence gets SXML_STATUS_INVALID_ARGUMENT instead of reentry.
Emptiness is get_item(0): at most one item of a lazy sequence is produced, and its error is reported ().
